_status: PRE-REGISTERED 2026-11-24 before any comparison with the lead's by-eye counts. All values are policy (ours), not published standards.

grid.note: every 2nd frame = 12 fps; ray grid at pixel centres

wall_dominated.rule: share of rays whose first opaque hit is < near_m is >= min_near_share

blocked.centre_window: middle half of columns and rows

outward.rule: rays that pass through glass first, or hit ground/context, or hit nothing

backward.note: stationary frames (holds, 360 turns) are never backward

dark_proxy.rule: camera room has no glazing within 0.6 m of its rectangle, and the walkthrough uses one house-wide day exposure

full_360.rule: union of horizontal view intervals of frames inside the room within radius of one standing point

calibration_sampling: lead looked every 6 s of the 8 fps preview of every 3rd interior frame = every 144th interior path frame

wall_dominated_v2.rule: one wall/door/furniture element (not floor/ceiling) takes >= 0.5 of the rays and the frame's median hit distance is < 3.0 m; interior frames only

dark_proxy_v2.rule: no window/glazed-door glass is seen first (before any opaque hit, within 10 m) by >= 2 % of rays cast from the room centre or its four quarter points at eye height, 72 azimuths x pitches -10,0,10,20 deg

revisions.made_after: first full run on the old route (v1 numbers kept in report.calibration as *_v1) and looking at the contact sheet of the by-eye frames
changes: wall_dominated: v1 (distance < 1.2 m, registered per the brief) caught 3 % of frames against ~30 % by eye. Contact-sheet frames the lead would call wall (kids-a 720, 810; corridor 900; parents-bed 1980) are a single flat surface at 1.5-3 m with 40-70 % element share, which a 1.2 m cut cannot see. v2 adds single-surface dominance. This is a post-hoc change made after seeing the by-eye counts; it is flagged as such.

dark proxy: v1 (no glass within 0.6 m of the room rectangle) marked open-plan sub-rooms (kitchen-island, dining-side) dark although they sit in a daylit hall. v2 asks whether glazing is visible from the room.
blocked: a plain wall in the centre counts as wall_dominated, not blocked (a camera facing a wall at 0.5 m is wall-dominated); blocked is for furniture, doors or pillars in the middle of the view.
